scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original A2 test on Daniel's study plan; comprehension and small real-life decisions; draft.

questions.q: What is different about Daniel's plan this week?
choices: He plans to study only at the weekend.
He does some studying on more than one day.
He studies all night before the test.
He asks his sister to do his schoolwork.
questions.explanation: Daniel spreads his preparation across Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday.

questions.q: How does Daniel find out that he does not fully understand an idea?
choices: He looks at his science test mark.
He checks the time on his phone.
He reads the same notes all evening.
He tries to explain the idea to his sister.
questions.explanation: Explaining to his sister reveals where he needs to check his notes.

questions.q: What does Daniel do before looking at the answers on Wednesday?
choices: He reads another student's test.
He phones his teacher for help.
He attempts some questions himself.
He writes down only the easy facts.
questions.explanation: He tries questions without looking at the answers.

questions.q: Why is going to bed late a problem for Daniel?
choices: He feels tired when he needs to take the test.
He misses his sister's questions in the evening.
He cannot find the answers in his textbook.
He is not allowed to study on Wednesday.
questions.explanation: His previous late-night study left him tired the next day.

questions.q: Why does Daniel switch off notifications while studying?
choices: To make his phone charge more quickly.
To help his sister use her own phone.
To make it easier to concentrate on his work.
To avoid getting any messages after school.
questions.explanation: Notifications distract Daniel from the questions he wants to practise.

questions.q: What is most important to Daniel after the test?
choices: He has improved his result and feels better prepared.
His teacher has given him a perfect score.
He has finished studying every school subject.
He no longer needs to prepare for history.
questions.explanation: Daniel values feeling calm and rested as well as the slightly improved grade.

questions.q: Your notes are confusing. What could Daniel's method help you do?
choices: Copy the notes without reading them.
Try explaining one idea and check what is unclear.
Stop practising until the night before the test.
Look at all the answers before trying questions.
questions.explanation: Daniel learns what he does not understand by explaining an idea and checking his notes.

questions.q: Your new method helps, but you still make a mistake. What could you do next?
choices: Decide the method is not useful.
Only study the questions you already know.
Forget the mistake and study nothing else.
Write down what to practise for next time.
questions.explanation: Daniel notes what he still needs to practise after the test.

questions.q: Daniel wants to use his plan for history. What should he remember?
choices: Every test needs exactly the same study time.
He can change the plan if it does not work well.
He should only use the plan for science.
A good plan means never making a mistake.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph says Daniel will make changes if needed.

questions.q: Which advice best matches the end of Daniel's story?
choices: A high mark matters more than sleep.
Study longer when you feel very tired.
Never change a plan that once worked.
A useful routine should help learning and well-being.
questions.explanation: Daniel appreciates a little improvement and the benefit of rest and a calmer evening.

sourceTitle: A Small Change, a Better Result
